beliefs.practice: Read the cluster connection string from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI) at runtime and never commit it to source control or log it.
Require TLS/SSL for all connections and validate server certificates (set tls/ssl=true and tlsInsecure/sslInvalid=false or equivalent) to prevent MITM attacks.
Create and reuse a single MongoClient per process (or application-wide client), rely on its connection pool, and close it cleanly on shutdown.
Configure sensible timeouts (connectTimeoutMS, serverSelectionTimeoutMS, socketTimeoutMS) so the app fails fast on network issues and avoids blocking indefinitely.
Enable/attempt retryable writes where supported and implement client-side exponential-backoff retries for transient errors and 429 (throttling) responses.
Make seed operations idempotent by using upserts (replace_one or update_one with upsert=True) so repeated runs do not create duplicates.
Limit the sample app to a dedicated database name (sample_banking_11) and ensure the client credentials only can access that database to reduce blast radius.
Provision sufficient throughput (RU/s or cluster tier) for indexing and query traffic, monitor 429s, and prefer autoscale or increase capacity if you see throttling during seeding or queries.
Create indexes on fields used in filters and sorts (e.g., correspondent_id unique index, entity_type, created_at, risk_score) and use compound indexes for common query patterns.
Store embeddings as dense numeric arrays (float32) in a dedicated field (e.g., 'embedding') and ensure the vector index you create matches that field and the embedding dimensionality.

When creating vector indexes, set the index type and parameters to match workload (choose HNSW/IVF/DiskANN appropriately) and explicitly set 'dimensions' to the embedding length and the distance metric (cosine or l2).
Normalize embeddings (unit length) if you will use cosine similarity, or consistently use the metric your index is configured for, so comparisons are correct.
Avoid returning full embeddings for non-search API responses: store or project them separately and use projection to exclude embedding bytes when not needed to reduce bandwidth and memory usage.
Use pagination (limit + skip or preferably cursor/continuation tokens) for listing results and avoid reading entire collections into memory.
Use deterministic synthetic embeddings in unit tests when API keys are not available so tests are repeatable and do not depend on external services.
Never write the connection string or API keys into logs, test artifacts, or README files; provide a .env.example with placeholders instead.
Use least-privilege database users: grant only read/write on the sample database and avoid giving cluster-admin or databaseAdmin roles to the application account.
Instrument and monitor query performance (use explain(), slow query logging, and index stats) and iterate on indexes before relying on client-side filtering or full scans.

For hybrid searches (vector similarity + metadata filters), apply selective metadata filters first (server-side) to narrow candidates, then perform nearest-neighbour search or re-rank results by vector score.
Choose appropriate readPreference and writeConcern (e.g., w='majority' for important writes) to match your consistency and durability requirements.
Store numeric fields (risk_score, match_count) using numeric types and store timestamps as ISODate; index timestamps if you will run retention or time-windowed queries.
Use TTL indexes for ephemeral or retention-based collections (e.g., raw scraped adverse-media items older than N days) to control storage costs and keep indexes small.
Enforce embedding dimensionality and basic schema constraints at insert time (application-side or via MongoDB schema validation) so malformed vectors are rejected early.
Have a tested backup and restore plan (mongodump/mongorestore or provider backups) and verify restores periodically for the sample database before relying on production data patterns.

If server-side hybrid vector search is not available or sufficient, pre-filter candidates server-side and perform approximate nearest-neighbour search with a well-tested client-side ANN library, but prefer server-side indexes for scale.
